extracted.intended_audience: comedy writers / late-night writers / stand-up comedians writing list jokes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing David Letterman-style Top Ten lists: one setup with ten punchlines that escalate (weak→strong) and culminate in a concise, summative #1. Covers word choice, rhythm, ordering, topical hooks, and writers' workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure: one setup → ten punchlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the Top Ten list as a single joke composed of one setup and ten punchlines; counts down from #10 (warmup) to #1 (peak).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The countdown itself is structural: #10 functions as a warmup and smaller laughs, climbing through the list to a peak at #1. Writers should conceive of the whole list as 'a joke with 10 punchlines' so that each item serves the unified setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently funny words
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer words that carry comedy on their own (words/phrases guaranteed to elicit laughs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'pants,' 'ass,' celebrity names like 'Regis' or historical comics like 'Ed Sullivan.' Favor hard consonants (K-sounds). Use specific brand names paired with ridiculous attributes to generate immediate laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final joke strategy (#1 placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: #1 should be the strongest line — often the shortest and serving as a summation or finality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the closing line concise and punchy; avoid making #1 too long or overly specific. It should provide a sense of closure and be easily quotable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm and variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary length and rhythm across items so the list feels like a meal or piece of music with movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't place two long items back-to-back. Mix short, rapid punches with longer, more elaborate setups to maintain audience attention and momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation and plot twists
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the numbered format to escalate humor and to set up expectations that can be subverted with twists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience anticipates increasing intensity; use escalation (weak→strong) and occasional subversions (e.g., '8 and a half') or rare meta breaks to surprise and heighten laughs. Plan beats so each number feels like progress toward the payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common topical hooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchor lists in readily recognizable topical material to increase immediacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective hooks include current celebrities or political figures, recent events, and universal fears or embarrassments. Topicality helps audience identification and makes jokes feel fresh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writers' approach / ingredient-generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce a large pool of candidate lines, then cull and order to the top ten.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate 50–100 candidates, then reduce to the best ten. Order items from weakest to strongest, reserving the single strongest, most summative line for #1. Consider adding a short 'tag' at the very end if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why the format works (audience mechanics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Top Ten format succeeds because it combines predictability with variation and built-in audience anticipation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits: predictable format with infinite variation, built-in audience anticipation for each numbered reveal, ease of reference/quoting, and a strong final line that is memorable. Use these strengths when choosing topics and crafting lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric: unifying topic specificity and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the unifying topic specific and clear?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list should hang on a single, well-defined topic so each item reads as a variant under that umbrella; vague or unfocused topics dilute impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric: use of inherently funny words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for the presence of words/phrases that generate laughs by sound or cultural resonance (see guidance on hard consonants, brand-name absurdities, and explicit examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric: list builds (weak to strong)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the list build from weaker items to stronger ones?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the sequence escalates effectively and whether earlier items set up the momentum toward progressively bigger laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric: #1 is strongest, shortest, summative
rubrics_metrics.description: Is #1 the strongest, shortest, and most summative line?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify #1 provides closure and is the clearest, most quotable payoff. It should summarize or amplify the premise rather than introduce an unrelated detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric: rhythm varied (not all same length)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the rhythm varied so items are not all the same length?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for alternation of short and long items, avoidance of repetitive sentence length, and placement that prevents two long setups appearing consecutively.
